pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Drop Down is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Walk into a crate to break it. Plop and Pip, the round friends that sit on the crates, hurt nobody, and nothing else in this game does either. For crates on their own see Smash It.

pages.head: Level 1: In the Way
pages.html:
Level 1: In the Way

The first sign, PLOP SITS ON A CRATE AND BLOCKS THE WAY, stands before a brick mound with a tunnel through it. In the tunnel a crate stands over a one-block dip in the floor, with Plop sitting on the crate. Plop is solid and the roof is low, so Lena can neither walk through it nor hop over it.

BREAK THE CRATE AND WHAT SITS ON IT FALLS says what to do. Walk into the crate: it turns to rubble and Plop drops two blocks into the dip, its back level with the floor. Lena walks over it. The last sign, MONSTERS HAVE NO GRAVITY. PLOP STEPS DOWN OVER AND OVER, says why it fell.

There are six coins, three in the tunnel and three beyond it.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Monsters have no gravity. Only Lena does. Game-Maker's monster file has a field called fly, "whether gravity has an effect on a monster", but the game never reads it. A monster goes only where its Movement sends it. So Plop falls with a Movement of its own.
  • The path. Open dd.mon in the monsters editor and pick Plop. Its Movement is Follows its path, with two corners. The first corner is the monster's own square. The second is one block straight down, at speed 20. The path is walked again and again, so Plop is always trying to take one more step down.
  • Stopped by solid blocks. Plop has this ticked. A solid block under it stops every step, so on a crate it sits still. When the crate becomes rubble, the next step is free and Plop drops, a block at a time, until something solid is under it. Untick it and Plop would fall through the floor.
  • The speed. The corner's speed is how many pixels it moves each tick: 20 is a whole block, so Plop crosses a block in a tick and lands before Lena can walk in underneath. Level 2 slows it down.
  • The frames. Plop has two pictures in dd.mbl, plop0 with its eyes open for about a second and plop1 with them shut for a blink. Its Pictures list gives each a time in ticks.
  • Solid. In dd.mbl, plop0 and plop1 are solid on every side, and take no hit points, so touching Plop never hurts. Its power is 110, so touching Lena does not pop it.
  • The crate and the dip. Open one.map in the map editor. The crate is the same block as in Smash It: solid on every side, and its Becomes block is rubble. The dip is one square of sky in the grass. Plop is one monster placed on the map, on top of the crate.

pages.head: Level 2: Slow and Soft
pages.html:
Level 2: Slow and Soft

PIP IS THE SAME TRICK, BUT SLOW AND SOFT comes first, then BREAK BOTH CRATES AND WATCH PIP DRIFT DOWN, before a tunnel with two crates stacked in it and a pink friend, Pip, on top. Walk in: Lena touches both crates, they turn to rubble, and Pip drifts down two blocks, a little at a time. It does not stop Lena. They can stand still and Pip sinks right through them, then lands on the floor behind them.

HOW FAST IT FALLS AND IF IT IS SOLID ARE SETTINGS comes after the tunnel, before three coins and the door. There are six coins in all.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The same Movement, slower. In dd.mon, Pip has exactly Plop's path: two corners, the second one block down. Only the speed on the corners is different: 2 pixels a tick, so a block takes ten ticks. Pip drifts. Change it to 20 and it drops like Plop.
  • Soft. In dd.mbl, pip0 and pip1 have no solid sides, so Lena passes through Pip, and Pip passes through them. A solid monster that lands on the hero can push them through the floor, so keep Lena out of its landing square, or make it soft.
  • Two crates. Lena is two blocks tall, so walking in touches both crates, which are stacked in the tunnel, and both break at once. Pip sits on the top one, so it falls two blocks.
  • Different, not the same. Pip is monster 4 and Plop monster 3, each with its own pictures and its own path, which is why one can be slow and soft and the other fast and solid. The crates and the tunnel are in two.map.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • A monster has no gravity. Falling is a path made to look like it. Lena's own gravity speeds up as they fall; a monster's speed is the same all the way down.
  • It only goes straight down. A monster does not slide off an edge or fall past one. It steps down where it is.
  • It never looks at the floor. It is always trying to step down; the solid block under it only stops the step.
  • A monster that lands touches nothing. It does not break a crate, press a switch or pick up a coin. Only Lena touches blocks.
  • Solid monsters can push Lena through the floor. If Plop lands where Lena stands, Lena can end up inside the ground. Here, level 1 drops Plop fast and Lena cannot walk in under it in time.
  • A broken block does not drop the blocks above. Crates and bricks never fall; only a monster does.
  • It cannot wait for you. It starts to fall within a tick or two of the block going.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Set Plop's corner speed to 2 and watch it fall slowly.
  • Untick Plop's Stopped by solid blocks and watch it fall through the floor of the dip.
  • Make Pip solid by giving pip0 and pip1 solid sides.
  • Move the crate somewhere else in one.map and put Plop on it.
  • Make the dip deeper.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
